Merge coincident vertices in a pool

Source: R/merge_coincident.R
merge_coincident.Rd

Merge coincident vertices in a pool

Usage

merge_coincident(x, tolerance = 0, period_x = NULL)

Arguments

x

A wkpool, or a wkpool_tri (see pool_triangulate())

tolerance

Numeric tolerance for coordinate matching. Default 0 means exact match only.

period_x

NULL (default) for no wrapping, or a single positive number: x is treated as periodic with this period when deciding which vertices coincide (for example 360 for longitude in degrees). See 'Periodic x' below.

Value

A wkpool (or wkpool_tri) with shared vertices merged (fewer unique vertices)

Details

With tolerance = 0, only exactly identical coordinates are merged - identity is the double-precision bit pattern (grouped at C level via vctrs), not a formatted representation, so values that differ only beyond printable precision remain distinct. The first occurrence becomes the canonical vertex; coordinates are never moved.

With a nonzero tolerance, coordinates are snapped to a grid of cell size tolerance for matching (the canonical vertex keeps its original coordinates). Note this is a snap grid, not a distance guarantee: two vertices within tolerance of each other that straddle a grid-cell boundary do not merge.

When the pool carries z, vertices are keyed on all coordinate columns: equal x/y with different z remain distinct vertices.

This is where you discover shared boundaries between polygons, network connectivity, mesh topology, etc.

Periodic x

With period_x set, vertices are keyed on x %% period_x (then on the tolerance snap grid, if any, wrapped again so that the grid cell at the period boundary is the same cell as the one at zero). This fuses the two copies of a seam, for example x = -180 and x = 180 for longitude, and with period_x = 360 data in a 0 to 360 convention fuses at 0 and 360 in the same way. Once fused, a seam is an ordinary internal boundary: find_shared_edges(), find_internal_boundaries() and the quotient argument of find_arcs() treat it like any other shared boundary.

The period is never inferred: wkpool carries the crs without interpreting it, so it cannot know that x is longitude. The decision to fuse is made here, explicitly.

Coordinates are still never moved: the canonical vertex keeps the x of its first occurrence (say -180), and segments from the other side of the seam now reference it. The topology is correct on the cylinder, but geometry emitted from the pool (for example by cycles_to_wkb()) has coordinate jumps of about one period across the seam. Consumers that understand wrapping (s2, great-circle densification) are fine; a planar consumer needs the seam split again downstream.

Segments are identified by their two vertices, so on the cylinder a segment cannot say which way round it goes. Two segments whose ends fuse to the same pair but which run opposite ways around become the same edge, for example the edge from -180 to 0 in one feature and from 0 to 180 in another. This needs a segment that spans at least half the period, so densify long segments before merging with period_x.

Only x is periodic. Poles (where all x coincide on the sphere), periodic y, and any detection from the crs are out of scope.

Feature provenance (.feature) is preserved - segments keep their original feature assignment even after vertex merging.

Examples

x <- wk::as_wkb(c(
  "POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 1, 0 0))",
  "POLYGON ((1 0, 2 0, 2 1, 1 1, 1 0))"
))
pool <- establish_topology(x)
topology_report(pool)
#> $n_vertices_raw
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $n_vertices_unique
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> $n_duplicate_vertices
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $n_near_miss_vertices
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $n_segments
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> $n_shared_edges
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_features
#> [1] 2
#> 
merged <- merge_coincident(pool)
topology_report(merged)
#> $n_vertices_raw
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> $n_vertices_unique
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> $n_duplicate_vertices
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $n_near_miss_vertices
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $n_segments
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> $n_shared_edges
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_features
#> [1] 2
#> 

# two hemispheres, each with its own copy of the antimeridian
g <- wk::as_wkb(c(
  "POLYGON ((-180 -60, 0 -60, 0 60, -180 60, -180 -60))",
  "POLYGON ((0 -60, 180 -60, 180 60, 0 60, 0 -60))"
))
pool <- establish_topology(g)
nrow(pool_vertices(merge_coincident(pool)))
#> [1] 6
fused <- merge_coincident(pool, period_x = 360)
nrow(pool_vertices(fused))
#> [1] 4
find_shared_edges(fused)
#>   edge_key .vx0 .vx1 .feature segment_idx features
#> 1      1-2    1    2        1           1     1, 2
#> 2      2-3    2    3        1           2     1, 2
#> 3      3-4    3    4        1           3     1, 2
#> 4      1-4    1    4        1           4     1, 2
#> 5      1-2    1    2        2           5     1, 2
#> 6      1-4    1    4        2           6     1, 2
#> 7      3-4    3    4        2           7     1, 2
#> 8      2-3    2    3        2           8     1, 2
